messages:
devon: Quick follow-up on the continuous batcher work — I want to propose a slot-centric admission model instead of the lane approach we sketched. Rationale: slots let us reason about headroom and KV cache residency per GPU more directly, and make preemption semantics simpler.

anya: Can you sketch how slots differ from lanes in runtime terms?

devon: Sure. Lanes are logical priority queues that mix requests of different sizes. Slots are fixed execution windows (n tokens / m ms) that we try to fill with compatible requests. Admission becomes: does the request fit an existing slot? if not, can we open a hot-slot? Slots also carry metadata: tenant budget, deadline_hint, and cache_affinity.

mike: Sounds interesting. How do we handle long-running streaming requests that continuously append tokens? Do they hog slots?

devon: Good point. Proposal: streaming gets a sticky slot id but with a token budget refill every X ms. If budget exhausted, we either spill to a lower-priority slot (degraded tail latency) or throttle. This avoids a single stream starving batch throughput.

jordan: What about preemption? One issue with lane-based preemption was starvation when many small requests preempt big ones repeatedly. With slots, can we do soft preempt: move large request to the next slot boundary and backfill?

devon: Exactly. Soft-preempt: a long request gets split at safe transformer checkpoints (kv cache boundary). We attempt to finish the current microbatch, then yield the slot for high-priority short work and resume in the next slot. This minimizes wasted compute and cache churn.

anya: Need to think about correctness with cache affinity. If we keep bouncing a model's KV cache, perf drops. Maybe we add a cache_affinity_score and prefer slots that keep the same model shards active.

mike: What admission policy? credit-based? tokens? deadline hints?

devon: Combine them. Admission checks (in order): 1) tenant_credit >= estimated_slot_cost 2) slot with compatible model/quantization exists or cold-open allowed 3) deadline_hint fits slot_end - now. If any fail -> apply fallback (defer, throttle, route to cheaper variant).

infra-bot: Deployment note: prototype change will touch runtime.admission and runtime.coalescer. Rolling flag recommended.

jordan: How do we expose tuning knobs to customers vs keeping default automatic? We don't want everyone fiddling with slot size.

devon: Defaults auto-configure using workload histogram (seq_len, tokens/sec) per tenant. Expose: max_slot_tokens, slot_time_ms, priority_buckets, and a boolean deadline_hint_opt_in. Defaults should work 90% of cases.

anya: Metrics we need to track in the Console: slot_utilization, avg_wait_per_slot, cancellation_due_to_credit, cache_affinity_score, preemptions_per_hour. Also a per-tenant slot_starvation alert.

mike: I'd add tail_latency_by_slot_type and kv_cache_evictions/sec.

devon: Agreed. Also need an offline simulator to model throughput vs latency with different slot sizes. I'll spin up a small harness that replays traces and computes cost/latency.

jordan: Is there a quick config example for the admission API? Something like:

```
{
  "max_slot_tokens": 1024,
  "slot_time_ms": 25,
  "priority_buckets": ["interactive","batch","background"],
  "credit_policy": "leaky_bucket",
  "deadline_hint_opt_in": true
}
```

devon: Yes, that's the idea. For prototyping I'd add a field on run_request: `deadline_hint_ms` and `cache_affinity_tag`.

anya: Caveat: we need to update model variant selector because some quantized variants have very different slot cost. Admission must use variant-cost estimates.

devon: Good catch. We'll store variant_cost_estimates in the model catalog and consult that during admission.

mike: Implementation plan? I'm happy to help on the simulator and metrics plumbing.

devon: Plan: (1) Simulator + offline tuning harness (2 weeks), (2) runtime admission prototype behind flag (2-3 weeks), (3) small canary on Dedicated with conservative defaults (1 week), (4) gather metrics, iterate.

jordan: SGTM. One more: we should ensure the slot model composes with existing autoscaler and capacity planner. Slots should be an execution layer primitive, autoscaler should see slot_utilization signals.

devon: Yup — autoscaler inputs: avg_slot_fill_rate, unserved_requests_build_up, and eviction_rate. I'll add a doc with API contracts.

anya: Thanks. Can you post the RFC follow-up with the simulator results when ready? :thumbsup:

devon: Will do. I'll open a short RFC and link the simulator repo when it's up.

infra-bot: New RFC created: /rfc/slot-centric-admission (draft) by devon — please review.
